newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges transitional government in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France urges transitional government in Zaire.

text.p: France on Tuesday urged the formation of a transitional government in war-torn Zaire, virtually abandoning its long-time ally President Mobutu Sese Seko as rebels headed towards Kinshasa.
"The creation of a transitional government should mark the start of national reconciliation," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.
He said a transitional government's first task would be "setting into effect, as soon as possible, the essential electoral process."
Rummelhardt said President Jacques Chirac's adviser on African affairs, Michel Dupuch, had met South African President Nelson Mandela in Pretoria on April 19 to lay out Paris' new position.

Dupuch also affirmed French support for South Africa's plan to organise a meeting between Mobutu and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, whose forces have seized half of Zaire's vast territory since taking up arms in October to topple Mobutu.

"The search for a negotiated solution is the only way out of the crisis," Rummelhardt said. "Any other way, notably the conquest of power by arms, would increase the suffering of the people and would raise the human toll."

France recently began distancing itself from Mobutu after backing him for most of his 32-year autocratic rule while urging the rebels to seek a peaceful settlement rather than carry out their threat to seize Kinshasa.
On Monday, Rummelhardt had hinted that Paris may be speaking to Kabila. "We are not ruling out any party in our contacts to solve the crisis," he said.
Zaire's government vowed on Monday its beleaguered army would never surrender Kinshasa and called on residents to be prepared for resistance.
